# AGENTS.md — Universal WebAssembly Bridge & Complete 16-App Command Catalog (`v0.1.0`)

This document is the authoritative agent & host integration reference for **`yubi-OS/craft-web-builds`**. It catalogs:
1. **All 4 Same-Origin & Cross-Frame Host Transport Modes** (`?host=parent`, `?embed`, `?host=<origin>`, `data-host="page"`),
2. **All JavaScript Global Interfaces** (`window.<app>` and `window.craftUniversalBridge`, including universal and app-specific methods),
3. **All 15 Incoming & 14 Outgoing `postMessage` / DOM `CustomEvent` Protocol Messages**,
4. **The Shared Agent Cursor Overlay & Dual-Path Frame Capture / WebRTC `MediaStream` API**,
5. **The 16-App Control-Channel Dialect & `docInspect` / `uiInspect` Schema Matrix**, and
6. **Every Single Command across All 16 ArtCraft WebAssembly Applications (8,835 commands total, 100% enriched with WebMCP JSON Schema `inputSchema`)**.

---

## 2. Host Transport Modes & URL Query Flags

Every WebAssembly build in this repository links `crates/craft-universal-bridge` (`universal_bridge.rs`, protocol version `universal/1`) and supports four host transport modes:

| Mode | Activation | Transport | Origin Validation & Framing Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`Parent`** | `?host=parent` | `window.parent.postMessage` | Requires a distinct parent `<iframe>` on the **same origin** (`window.parent.location.origin === window.location.origin`). Rejects opaque (`"null"`) origins. |
| **`Embed`** | `?embed` or `?embed=1` or `?embed=parent` | `window.parent.postMessage` | Same-origin parent `<iframe>`; adds `photocraftEmbed: 1` and `<app>Embed: 1` markers on outgoing messages and enables revision-gated `saveAck` tracking (`#9593`). |
| **`ExplicitOrigin`** | `?host=https://example.com` or `?embed=https://example.com` | `window.parent.postMessage` | Validates `event.origin` against the explicitly configured origin (`https://` or `http://localhost` / `http://127.0.0.1`). |
| **`Page`** | `data-host="page"` on `<canvas>` | DOM `CustomEvent` on `<canvas>` | Same-document, no `<iframe>` required. Host dispatches `new CustomEvent("<app>:<kind>", { detail: payload, bubbles: false })` on `<canvas>` and listens for `<app>:<kind>` events on `<canvas>`. |

### Additional URL Query Flags
- `?control` — Enables upstream `window.<app>` control channel (the Universal Bridge also installs `window.<app>` and `window.craftUniversalBridge` unconditionally).
- `?webgl` — Forces the WebGL2 backend (`eframe::wgpu::Backends::GL`), recommended for headless browsers (Puppeteer / Playwright with `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`).
- `?lang=<tag>` — Overrides the initial UI locale (e.g. `?lang=es`, `?lang=ja`, `?lang=zh-CN`).
- `?saveAck` — Requires explicit host `saved` / `saveAck` confirmation before clearing the dirty flag after a save.
- `?exam=1` — Enables exam/lock mode (`#1614`), blocking `file.open*`, `file.save*`, `file.export*`, `file.place*`, `file.import*`, `app.open*`, `app.save*`, `app.export*`.

## 3. JavaScript Global Interface (`window.<app>` & `window.craftUniversalBridge`)

Inside the application window (or via `iframe.contentWindow` from a same-origin parent page), both `window.<app>` and `window.craftUniversalBridge` expose a unified 14-method API:

| Method | Signature | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commands` | `commands()` | `Promise<Array<CommandInfo> \| {commands: Array<CommandInfo>}>` | Returns the full command catalog for the running app, with every command enriched with a WebMCP JSON Schema `inputSchema: { type: "object", properties, required, additionalProperties }`. |
| `execute` | `execute(commandId, params?)` | `Promise<any>` | Executes any engine or UI command by ID (`commandId`), automatically adapting between `engine.execute {command, params}`, `ui.command {id, params}`, and `command.run {id, params}` and incrementing the document revision counter on success. |
| `request` | `request(method, params?)` | `Promise<any>` | Sends a raw JSON control-channel request (`method`, `params`) and resolves with `reply.result` (or rejects with `Error(reply.error)`). Automatically wakes the `eframe` loop while in flight. |
| `docInspect` | `docInspect(params?)` | `Promise<object>` | Inspects the active document/session/drawing (`document.inspect` / `session.inspect` / `ui.state`). Automatically adapts if `document.inspect` is an engine command (`photocraft`) and falls back to `uiInspect` when no document is open. |
| `uiInspect` | `uiInspect(params?)` | `Promise<object>` | Inspects the live UI state, panels, dialogs, viewport/canvas geometry, and accessibility/widget tree (`ui.inspect`). |
| `inspect` | `inspect(params?)` | `Promise<object>` | Alias for `uiInspect(params)`. |
| `screenshot` | `screenshot(params?)` | `Promise<FrameSnapshot>` | Captures the current frame via `ui.screenshot` (with `HTMLCanvasElement.toDataURL("image/png")` fallback). |
| `captureFrame` | `captureFrame({ includeCursor?, ... }?)` | `Promise<{ width, height, data, png, cursor, revision }>` | Dual-path frame capture: captures the live canvas/viewport as base64 PNG (`data` / `png`) together with the current `cursor` state and `revision`. |
| `captureStream` | `captureStream(fps?)` | `MediaStream` | Invokes `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.captureStream(fps)` on the app's primary `<canvas>`, returning a live WebRTC `MediaStream` for real-time video streaming or `MediaRecorder` capture. |
| `setCursor` | `setCursor({ x, y, visible?, normalized?, pressed?, label?, color? })` | `CursorState` | Updates the shared agent cursor state and immediately positions/styles the non-blocking DOM overlay `#<canvas_id>_agent_cursor` above the canvas. |
| `getCursor` | `getCursor()` | `CursorState` | Returns the current shared agent cursor state `{ x, y, visible, normalized, pressed, label, color }`. |
| `pointer` | `pointer({ kind?, x?, y?, events?, space? })` | `Promise<any>` | Updates the shared agent cursor overlay AND forwards synthetic pointer/gesture events to the app's pointer control method (`ui.pointer` / `ui.input` / `ui.click`). |
| `saveAck` | `saveAck(revisionOrId)` | `boolean` | Confirms that the host persisted the save at `revision` (or `id`), clearing the dirty gate when `savedRevision >= currentRevision`. |
| `state` | `state()` | `{ app, bridgeVersion, dirty, revision, savedRevision, cursor }` | Synchronous snapshot of the bridge's revision/dirty state and shared agent cursor. |

## 4. Same-Origin Host Frame Protocol (`postMessage` & DOM `CustomEvent`)

All messages sent from the host frame to the app accept either `<app>:<kind>` (e.g. `photocraft:execute`), bare `<kind>` when accompanied by `bridge: "emu/1"`, `craftBridge: "universal/1"`, or `<app>Embed: 1`, or `craft:<kind>`.

### 4.1 Incoming Messages (Host → App)

| Kind (`<app>:<kind>`) | Aliases | Payload Fields | Response Message | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<app>:hello` | `host`, `ping` | `{ requestId? }` | `<app>:ready` | Handshake ping; causes the app to re-emit `<app>:ready` with capabilities and version metadata. |
| `<app>:open` | `open` | `{ name?, bytes: ArrayBuffer \| Uint8Array, fonts?: [{family, bytes}], requestId? }` | `<app>:opened` or `<app>:open-failed` | Opens a document/image/project from raw bytes in memory (up to 512 MiB) without a file picker. Sanitizes path traversal and control chars in `name`. |
| `<app>:save` | `export` | `{ format?, requestId? }` | `<app>:save` + `<app>:response` | Triggers a host-initiated save or export (`file.save` or registered `on_save_trigger` callback). |
| `<app>:saved` | `saveAck`, `save-ack` | `{ revision?: number, id?: string }` | `<app>:dirty` (if clean) | Confirms the host persisted the save at `revision`; clears `dirty` when no newer edits occurred since that save. |
| `<app>:picked` | `picked` | `{ name, handle? }` | — | Supplies the chosen filename for a pending `pick-save` dialog request (`#3101`). |
| `<app>:commands` | `commands` | `{ requestId? }` | `<app>:response` | Returns the full WebMCP-enriched command list under both `result` and `commands`. |
| `<app>:execute` | `cmd`, `command` | `{ command: string, params?: object \| string, requestId? }` | `<app>:response` | Executes any command by ID (`command` or `id`) with `params` (JSON object or JSON string) through the normalized dialect adapter. |
| `<app>:request` | `control` | `{ method: string, params?: object, requestId? }` | `<app>:response` | Executes any low-level control-channel method (`engine.commands`, `engine.execute`, `ui.inspect`, `ui.widgets`, `ui.screenshot`, etc.). |
| `<app>:inspect` | `docInspect`, `uiInspect`, `state` | `{ target?: "doc" \| "ui", params?: object, requestId? }` | `<app>:response` | Inspects document state (`target: "doc"` or omitted, with automatic fallback to `ui.inspect` when no document is open) or UI state (`target: "ui"`). |
| `<app>:cursor` | `cursor` | `{ x: number, y: number, visible?: boolean, normalized?: boolean, space?: "normalized", pressed?: boolean, label?: string, color?: string }` | — | Moves/updates the shared agent cursor overlay `#<canvas_id>_agent_cursor` in real time. |
| `<app>:pointer` | `input` | `{ kind?, x?, y?, events?: Array<{kind, x, y}>, space?, requestId? }` | `<app>:response` | Updates the shared agent cursor overlay AND injects synthetic pointer/gesture input into the app. |
| `<app>:snapshot-request` | `snapshotRequest`, `screenshot`, `capture` | `{ includeCursor?: boolean, requestId? }` | `<app>:snapshot` | Captures the current frame and replies with both base64 `data` and a zero-copy transferred `ArrayBuffer` (`bytes`), plus `width`, `height`, `cursor`, and `revision`. |
| `<app>:exam` | `lock` | `{ on?: boolean }` | — | Locks or unlocks file open/save/export/place/import commands (`#1614` exam mode). |
| `<app>:autosave` | `autosave` | `{ intervalMs?: number }` | — | Configures or disables (`<= 0`) periodic autosave interval (clamped to `[5000, 3600000]` ms). |
| `<app>:handoff-done` | `handoffDone` | `{ id? }` | — | Acknowledges completion of a cross-app asset handoff. |

### 4.2 Outgoing Messages (App → Host)

Every outgoing message includes `type: "<app>:<kind>"`, `kind: "<kind>"`, `app: "<app>"`, `craftBridge: "universal/1"`, and `bridge: "emu/1"` (plus `photocraftEmbed: 1` and `<app>Embed: 1` in `?embed` mode).

| Kind (`<app>:<kind>`) | Payload Fields | Transfer List | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<app>:ready` | `{ version: "1", bridgeVersion: "universal/1", app, appVersion, formatExtension, rev, file: false, capabilities: string[] }` | — | Emitted once the WASM module, WebGL/WebGPU context, and Universal Bridge are ready. |
| `<app>:opened` | `{ ok: true, name, warnings: [], revision, requestId? }` | — | Emitted after `<app>:open` delivers bytes into the app's open inbox. |
| `<app>:open-failed` | `{ error: string }` | — | Emitted when `<app>:open` is missing bytes or exceeds the 512 MiB cap. |
| `<app>:save` | `{ name, saveAs: boolean, revision: number, bytes: ArrayBuffer, document: ArrayBuffer, requestId? }` | `[bytes]` | Zero-copy transferred `ArrayBuffer` of saved/exported file bytes with monotonic `revision` number. |
| `<app>:save-failed` | `{ error: string }` | — | Emitted when a save/export operation fails. |
| `<app>:dirty` | `{ dirty: boolean, revision: number }` | — | Emitted whenever the document dirty state changes. |
| `<app>:response` | `{ method, command, ok: boolean, result: any, commands: any, value: string, error: string \| null, revision: number, requestId?, id? }` | — | Unified response to `<app>:commands`, `<app>:execute`, `<app>:request`, `<app>:inspect`, `<app>:pointer`, and `<app>:save`. |
| `<app>:snapshot` | `{ ok: boolean, format: "png", width: number, height: number, data: string, bytes: ArrayBuffer, cursor: CursorState, revision: number, requestId? }` | `[bytes]` | Dual-path frame capture response carrying both base64 PNG (`data`) and zero-copy transferred `ArrayBuffer` (`bytes`). |
| `<app>:failed` | `{ error: string, id? }` | — | Startup or fatal operation error notification. |

## 6. Complete Command Catalog across All 16 Applications (8,835 Commands)

Every command below can be invoked from the same-origin host page via:
```js
// 1. Same-origin postMessage:
iframe.contentWindow.postMessage({
  type: "<app>:execute",
  requestId: "req-1",
  command: "<command-id>",
  params: { /* see Parameters column */ }
}, window.location.origin);

// 2. Or directly via window.<app> / window.craftUniversalBridge:
await iframe.contentWindow.craftUniversalBridge.execute("<command-id>", { /* params */ });
```

Automatically Create First Snapshot: a new or opened document starts with a snapshot of itself, named after it (default on). Automatically Create New Snapshot When Saving: each save of the document (not a copy) adds a snapshot named with the time of the save (default off). Allow Non-Linear History: an edit after stepping back keeps the later states and is appended at the end; deleting a state deletes only it (default off). Show New Snapshot Dialog by Default: a click on the History panel's camera button opens New Snapshot, not only ⌥-click (default off). Make Layer Visibility Changes Undoable: showing or hiding a layer is a history state (default on). Also `prefs.set historyOptions.*`` |

| `actions.setPlayback` | Playback Options | — | — | `{"performance":"accelerated"\\|"step"\\|"pause"?, "seconds":1..60?, "singleState":bool?} → {performance, seconds, singleState}. The Actions panel menu's Playback Options, saved in preferences (`actions.performance`, `actions.pauseSeconds`, `actions.createSingleHistoryState`). Step by Step and Pause For pace a person's Play in the app, about one second between steps plus Pause For's whole seconds; actions.play from agents, the CLI and Batch always runs at once. Omitted keys keep their value; {} reads them. Every value is checked before any is stored.` |
| `actions.move` | Move Action or Step | — | — | `{"action":name\\|index, "step":index?, "to":index}. Move a step within its action, or the action itself. to is the final zero-based index. Pending recorded steps can be moved.` |

| `actions.record` | Record Action | — | — | `{"name":str? (new action, default "Action N"),"set":name? (the set it goes in, as New Action records into the selected set)} or {"action":name\\|index} (append) → {action, index}` |

Stops at the first error (the command still returns ok, with failed set) and groups document edits in one Action: <name> history entry by default; actions.setHistory can retain per-step history. Nested calls are supported up to 16 levels; cycles are rejected. Recording stores a named call rather than its expanded commands. Each step is checked with Session::authorize when one is installed.` |
| `actions.delete` | Delete Action | — | — | `{"action":name\\|index, "step":index?} → {deleted:name} or {action, deletedStep, steps:count}. step is 0-based, including pending recorded steps. Whole-action deletion is refused while recording.` |
| `actions.toggle` | Toggle Action Steps | — | — | `{"action":name\\|index, "step":index?, "enabled":bool?} → {action, disabled:[step…]}. Switch one 0-based step (including pending recorded steps) on or off for playback, Batch and droplets; omitted enabled flips it. Without step, switch every step: on unless all already are, or as enabled says.` |

### 6.2 `vectorcraft` (`window.vectorcraft`) — 1,373 Commands

- **Canvas ID:** `#vectorcraft_canvas` (`#vectorcraft_canvas_agent_cursor` overlay)
- **Control Dialect:** commands=`engine.commands`, execute=`engine.execute {command, params}`, docInspect=`document.inspect`, uiInspect=`ui.inspect`, screenshot=`ui.screenshot`, pointer=`ui.pointer`

| `document.inspect` | Inspect Document | — | — | `{depth?, childLimit?, ids?: [id…] (list just these nodes, of any level, in this order, under `nodes` in place of `layers`; an unknown id is an error; at most 10000), kind?: panel label such as Layer; Group; Path; Type or Image (exact, ignoring case; list every such node under `nodes`, each with `path`, its ancestor ids with the layer first, searching the subtrees of `ids` when given), limit?: at most this many entries of the list, offset?: entries skipped first (default 0; with `ids`, `kind`, `limit` or `offset` the reply adds `total`, the entries before paging)} → layer tree (each node: id, name, kind, visible, locked, bounds, opacity (0–1) and opacityPct (0–100 %, the scale object.setProps takes) when below 1, blend when not Normal, fill, stroke and strokeWidth of objects and compound paths; a compound path's members have compoundMember: true instead of paint, which is the compound's), artboards, selection, history (a sliced tree reports childCount); without the scope options the reply is the whole layer tree` |

Saved with the document → {global}` |

The new document is named with the next Untitled-N, has nothing selected and no steps to undo or redo, is marked unsaved and links to the same files. It is out of symbol, opacity-mask and pattern editing, with the art drawn in a pattern's tile stored in the pattern as object.pattern.done stores it. The source document and its steps stay as they are, except that typing or a drag in progress is first kept as a step, as edit.undo keeps it; `index` names the row as it was listed before that. An index that names no state is an error and changes nothing → {index: the new document's, title}` |

| `edit.paste` | Paste | Edit | `Cmd+V` | `{center?: [x, y], artboardsAt?: [x, y], dx?, dy?, swatchConflict?} paste centred on `center` (the app passes the view centre), else offset by dx/dy (default: the Paste Offset preference). Pasting brings the image blobs, symbols, patterns, global and spot swatches (with the tint swatches of the tints used), gradient swatches, graphic styles, character and paragraph styles and brushes the objects use; one of the same name that differs comes in renamed. swatchConflict, for a swatch whose name the document gives another colour (clipboard.conflicts): "merge" (default: the objects take the document's swatch) \\| "add" (the pasted swatch comes in renamed) \\| {name: "merge"\\|"add"}. With Paste Remembers Layers on (layer.pasteRemembersLayers), objects go back into the layers they came from (by name; made when missing). Artboards copied with artboard.copy come with their art, together right of the last artboard as they lay, or centered on `artboardsAt` (the Artboard tool's canvas menu passes the right-click point; a value that is not [x, y] is an error) (the other paste commands but Paste on All Artboards: where they were), their art back in the layers it came from, and the Artboard tool, when chosen, selects them. In Draw Inside (view.drawMode) the objects go inside the object drawn into, as new art does, and Paste Remembers Layers doesn't apply; edit.pasteInPlace and edit.pasteOnAllArtboards do the same, and in Draw Behind they go behind the selection as edit.pasteInBack puts them; edit.pasteInFront and edit.pasteInBack ignore the drawing mode → {ids, artboard: the first new artboard's index or null, artboards: the new artboards' indices, added: resources added, merged: conflicts merged, renamed: [{kind, from, to}]}` |

with limitTo, art linked to the global or spot swatch the new color is takes this share of its tint)}] \\| {"key or #rrggbb": colour, …} (one row per colour), method?: "exact" (default)\\|"preserveTints"\\|"scaleTints"\\|"tintsShades"\\|"hueShift" (how a row's colours take its new colour, relative to the row's darkest, average or most saturated colour), limitTo?: swatch library id or name; or "document" (the document's swatches): new colours snap to its nearest colour, group?: colour group to rewrite, groupColors?: [colour] (what `group` is rewritten with; default: the rows' new colours, in order, excluded rows left out), rename?: the group's new name, includeImages?: true, includePatterns?: true, globalAdjust?: {saturation?: 0, brightness?: 0, temperature?: 0, luminosity?: 0} (Global Adjust: percent from -100 to 100, 0 changes nothing; every colour a row that isn't excluded recolours, and the group's new colours, take the same change after the row's new colour: saturation scales HSB saturation by 1 + saturation/100, brightness moves HSB brightness that share of the way to full or to black, temperature adds 0.2 × temperature/100 to red and takes it from blue, luminosity moves Lab lightness that share of the way to 100 or 0 keeping a and b; with limitTo each row's new colour takes the change before it snaps to the library)} recolour the selection (gradients, text, meshes, image pixels and pattern tiles included; each new colour keeps the model of the one it replaces (model?: "keep" default \\| "new" (the new colour's own model, so a CMYK colour replacing RGB art gives CMYK art) \\| "document" (the document's colour mode)), except a library swatch's with limitTo: art takes the swatch itself, linked to a global or spot colour at its tints, and the swatch joins the document's swatches; A search reads the table directories and the name, fvar and OS/2 tables of .ttf, .otf, .ttc and .otc files of at most 256 MB and, on macOS, of suitcase fonts (files without an extension or with .suit, whose fonts are in a resource fork of at most 8 MB), and lists a file for a font when the file, added with text.addFontFiles, makes the font resolve exactly as text.fonts resolves it; fonts that resolve exactly already are left out. It doesn't enter app packages, folders named Program Files (also x86 and Arm), ProgramData, $Recycle.Bin or System Volume Information, the system's folders at the root of a volume, the Shared and Public folders in Users, a home folder's Library, AppData, Applications, snap and dot folders, a Library folder's app data folders or the folders the environment names for apps' data, and a search of a folder inside one of them fails; the walk also skips other hidden folders, folders whose contents are in the cloud and folders more than 64 levels deep, and follows no links (a picked path is resolved through its links); none on the web → {id (absent while idle), state: idle\\|searching\\|done\\|stopped\\|failed, folder?, fonts: [{family, style, status, files: [paths]}], searched?: {folders, files, fontFiles}, skipped?, unreadable?, stopped?: stop\\|time\\|limit, error?, seconds?}` |
| `text.addFontFiles` | Add Font Files | — | — | `{files: [paths the last text.findFontFiles search found] (1 to 1000)} copy the font files into VectorCraft's own Fonts folder (next to the preferences; the desktop app and vectorcraft-cli read it), never replacing a file there: the names Name.otf, Name 2.otf … Name 99.otf are tried in turn until one is free, which gets the copy, or is a file with the same contents, which is kept; then scan the fonts again, as text.rescanFonts does, and type set in them redraws. Only regular .ttf, .otf, .ttc, .otc, .woff and .woff2 files and suitcase fonts (with their resource fork) are copied, at most 256 MB a file and 1 GB in all; any other file is skipped. Add only fonts you own or are licensed to install; none on the web → {folder, copied: [{from, to}], kept: [{from, to}], skipped: [{file, reason}], families?, faces?}` |

The document's variables and their bindings stay. A header that names no variable defines one, unbound: `#Name` defines a visibility variable, `@Name` defines an image variable, and a header without a prefix defines a text variable. A prefixed header whose name is a variable of another kind, and a `%` header that isn't a variable's exact name (graph data files), are refused, and so are two headers that name one variable and a header that would define a variable while the variables are locked. Every data set is deleted, and every variable of the document is deleted with its bindings and values except a text variable the library also declares, which keeps its bindings; then the library's other variables whose `trait` is `textcontent` are defined as text variables, unbound, and each data set takes a value for a variable from the `p` elements of the element named after it, one paragraph each. Variables of other kinds are left out and named in `skipped` and `warning`. Refused while the variables are locked when it would delete or define a variable → {variables, deleted, deletedDataSets, names, skipped, warning?}` |

Variables of other kinds are left out with their values and named in `skipped` and `warning`. Refused without a text variable, for a text variable whose name isn't an XML name (letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, starting with a letter or `_`), for a data set name or value that holds a control character, for a data set name with white space at either end, for a name longer than 255 characters or used twice, and past variable.loadLibrary's caps (256 variables, 1,000 data sets, 8 MiB). Without path → {xml, variables, datasets, skipped, warning?}; with it → {path, variables, datasets, skipped, warning?}` |

When the marker's tab went to the left indent, the paragraph gets a left-aligned tab stop without a leader there, in place of any stop there, which keeps the text after the tab where it started; when it went to a tab stop and a stop there or past it has a leader or is not left-aligned, or a right, center or decimal stop lies between the marker and that place, the paragraph gets a left-aligned stop without a leader where the marker's tab ended, in place of any stop there and of those right, center and decimal stops before it (past the left indent only in a paragraph with no tab of its own). In threaded type the numbers are those counted through the story's frames, and a paragraph that continues into a later frame is converted where its text starts. An empty list paragraph has no marker and only leaves the list. A paragraph with no direction set gets the direction it ran in when the characters would change it (a letter or roman numeral before right-to-left text). With the Every-line Composer, a paragraph with a tab is broken line by line, so a converted paragraph can break its lines at other places. While the Type tool edits, its typing ends first and its anchor and caret move past the characters inserted at or before them (a whole story that Select All selected stays selected when the call converts all of it); in threaded type, when the caret's character moved to another frame, the tool edits that frame, which becomes the selection when it was not selected. random: between a and b; pressure: a at the lightest pen pressure to b at the heaviest; tilt: a with the pen lying flat to b upright; bearing and rotation: a at −180° to b at 180°), rotation_relative_to_path. art: width 1..1000%, width_mode: null (fixed)\\|pressure, width_max 1..1000% (pressure: width at the lightest pen pressure to width_max at the heaviest, half way on a stroke drawn without pressure), scale: {mode: proportional\\|stretch\\|betweenGuides, start, end: 0..1 of the art length}, direction: leftToRight\\|rightToLeft\\|topToBottom\\|bottomToTop, flip_along, flip_across, overlap. pattern: scale 1..10000%, spacing 0..10000%, fit: stretch\\|addSpace\\|approximate, flip_along, flip_across, outer_corner and inner_corner: corner tile art (drawn as the corner that joins a side tile on its right to one below it) or null, outer_source and inner_source: what that kind of corner draws without its art: none\\|autoCentered\\|autoBetween\\|autoSliced\\|autoOverlap (a tile made from the side tile), or null (the other kind of corner's art); side_tile, outer_corner_tile, inner_corner_tile, start_tile, end_tile: a document pattern name, original, or none (side refuses none); corner tiles also take autoCentered\\|autoBetween\\|autoSliced\\|autoOverlap. | `document.exportPdf` | Export PDF | — | — | `{path?, preset?: "VectorCraft Default" (built-in or saved: pdf.preset.list), artboard? \\| artboards?: [i…] \\| range?: "1-3, 5" (1-based; default all, one page each), standard?: none\\|pdfA2b\\|pdfX1a (CMYK, grey and spot colours only: colours and images converted to output.destination or the CMYK output intent, untagged; transparency flattened with flattenerPreset; PDF 1.3)\\|pdfX3 (colours ICC-tagged; transparency flattened; PDF 1.3)\\|pdfX4 (transparency and layers kept; colours ICC-tagged; PDF 1.6 at most) (PDF/X: a /GTS_PDFX output intent, by default the CMYK profile in effect, embedded; TrimBox, Trapped, GTS_PDFXVersion, title and dates; fonts embedded or outlined), compatibility?: 1.3 (no transparency: it is flattened with flattenerPreset; images keep no see-through pixels)\\|1.4\\|1.5\\|1.6\\|1.7 (default)\\|2.0 (choosing a standard sets its version: 1.7 for pdfA2b, 1.6 for pdfX4, 1.3 for pdfX1a and pdfX3, which write 1.4 as 1.3 too; pdfA2b refuses 1.3), preserveEditing? (on in VectorCraft Default: the native document as an embedded file, which document.open restores; choosing a standard turns it off, a standard refuses it), thumbnails? (each page drawn as a /Thumb image, 106 px on its long side), fastWebView? (a linearised file: the first page shows while the rest downloads; it stays linearised when encrypted), viewAfterSaving? (the app opens the written file), createLayers? (each layer and sublayer but template layers as a PDF layer, an optional content group listed under its layer's: hidden layers off, non-printing ones /PrintState /OFF, locked ones locked; needs 1.5 or later; they reopen as layers; choosing pdfX1a or pdfX3 turns it off; they refuse it), includeNonPrinting? (keep layers whose Print option is off; left out by default unless createLayers), flattenerPreset?: "" (High Resolution) \\| high \\| medium \\| low \\| a saved preset (flattener.presets.list): what PDF 1.3 files flatten transparency with, flattener?: {object.flattenTransparency options over it}, compression?: {color?, gray?: {downsample: none\\|average\\|subsample\\|bicubic, ppi: 300, abovePpi: 450, compression: none\\|zip\\|jpeg\\|jpeg2000\\|auto, quality: minimum\\|low\\|medium\\|high\\|maximum}, mono?: {downsample, ppi: 1200, abovePpi: 1800, compression: none\\|ccittG3\\|ccittG4\\|zip\\|runLength} (black-and-white images), compressText?: true} (images above abovePpi are resampled to ppi; auto keeps JPEGs JPEG, the others lossless; JPEG needs opaque images; none, jpeg2000, CCITT and runLength are written as ZIP with a warning), marks?: {trim, registration, colorBars, pageInfo, kind: roman\\|japanese, weight: 0.25 (trim marks and targets), offset: 6 (pt from the artboard, at least the bleed)} (printer's marks in [Registration], every plate: trim marks, registration targets mid-side, CMYK/spot/black-tint colour bars on top, page information (title, artboard, date UTC) below), bleed?: {useDocument (the document's bleed, document.setup), top, bottom, left, right} (pt; art in the bleed is kept; a PDF/X file with no bleed on a side where the document's bleed has one comes back with a warning). Each page: TrimBox = artboard, BleedBox = artboard + bleed, MediaBox = that + the marks' room (art clipped to the BleedBox), output?: {conversion: none (default)\\|destination (every colour into the destination profile's model, CMYK or RGB, also colours of that model in another profile)\\|preserveNumbers (only colours of the other model and Lab; those in the destination's model keep their numbers) (grey stays grey; images are converted too, printer's marks are not), destination: profile name (edit.colorSettings lists them; default: the document's profile for its colour mode), profiles: none (device colours)\\|all\\|destination\\|taggedSource (documents assigned a profile: edit.assignProfile) (ICC-based colours: CMYK with the destination or document CMYK profile, RGB as sRGB, grey with the sRGB tone curve; PDF/A, pdfX3 and pdfX4 always, whatever profiles says), outputIntent: profile name (embedded as the catalog's /GTS_PDFX output intent; a name that isn't a profile is only named, which pdfX1a and pdfX3 allow only with a registry and pdfX4 refuses; pdfX1a needs a CMYK one), outputCondition, outputConditionId (default: outputIntent), registry, trapped (/Trapped /True; /False when an output intent is written)} (PDF/A files keep their own output intent), advanced?: {fontSubsetPercent: 100 (below 100 is accepted with a warning: fonts are always embedded as subsets), outlineText: false (type as real, selectable and searchable text in embedded subset fonts with a ToUnicode map; fonts whose licence forbids embedding, or allows only whole fonts, stay outlines with a warning; true: every glyph as an outline), overprint: preserve (overprinting fills and strokes set /OP /op true, /OPM 1; white ones knock out with document.setup discardWhiteOverprint)\\|discard (they knock out)}, security?: {openPassword, permissionsPassword, printing: none\\|low\\|high, changes: none\\|pages\\|forms\\|comments\\|any, copy, screenReader, plaintextMetadata}, acknowledgeLoss?: bool (write over the file the document was read from although reading it left things out), format?: "pdf"} → {path, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, bytes, warnings}. The options apply over the preset (null keeps its value); options accepted but not applied yet come back as warnings; a standard with a PDF version it doesn't allow and a password with a standard are refused, and so is a PDF/X file that would still break its standard (transparency the flattener left, RGB in pdfX1a, a font not embedded) or a PDF 1.3 file with transparency left. document.export {format: pdf} takes the same options` |

| `file.place` | Place… | File | `Cmd+Shift+P` | `{path \\| name \\| dataBase64 (a file's path, or its name with its bytes), link?: true (a raster image keeps its file's path; a VectorCraft document at path becomes one locked placed document showing artboard `page`, linked to the file and read again when it changes (links.update; saving it in this app updates it at once), drawn as vectors in every output; so does a PDF/.ai page at path, showing its `crop` box, unless password or textAs: "outlines" is given; false: an editable copy of its art, as from dataBase64; other files are embedded), text?: {characterSet?: "unicode" (UTF-8, or UTF-16 with a byte-order mark; other bytes as the platform's 8-bit set) \\| "ansi" (the platform's 8-bit set), platform?: "windows" (Windows-1252) \\| "mac" (Mac Roman), removeLineReturns?: false (each block of lines becomes one paragraph; blank lines end paragraphs), removeParagraphReturns?: false (drop blank lines), replaceSpaces?: n (runs of n ≥ 2 spaces become a tab)} (a .txt file, placed as area type filling rect, the replaced object's bounds, or else the artboard less a 36 pt margin), template?: false (onto a new locked template layer below the current layer), replace?: false (swap the one selected object, keeping its stacking place and transform; no at/rect), at?: [x, y] centre (default: the first artboard's centre), rect?: [x, y, width, height] fit inside; aspect kept (wins over at), page?: 1 (PDF/.ai page, or a native document's artboard), crop?: "crop" (clipped to that page or artboard, default; an SVG, only when given: framed and clipped by its viewBox, else by its art's bounds) \\| "bounding" (the bounds of the art that shows, with its strokes and effects, as an export measures them: hidden objects and guides left out) \\| "art" \\| "trim" \\| "bleed" \\| "media" (a PDF page's boxes), password? (an encrypted PDF), dxf?: {…the DXF options of document.open} (a .dxf drawing: fit fills the artboard under at, else the first; fitted or uncentred art lands with its drawing's artboard on that artboard, else it is centred on at)} → {ids, name, format, linked, width, height, warnings}. Raster images come in at 100% of their physical size (the file's ppi, else 72); SVG, DXF, PDF/.ai, EMF/WMF (clipped to the picture's frame), EPS (clipped to its bounding box; as document.open reads it), a .ai saved without PDF compatibility (from its editing data, as document.open reads it: the art of the layers that show on artboard `page`, clipped to that artboard unless crop is "bounding") and native documents as one group, with the images, symbols, patterns, swatches and brushes they use. One undo step; selects what it placed (unless on a template layer); never touches the clipboard. A PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image whose pixels can't be read (a file cut short) is an error, and nothing is placed` |

| `links.check` | Check Links | — | — | `{ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: every linked image and placed document)} where each linked file is and whether it changed since it was read → {links: [{name, path, status: ok\\|modified\\|missing, ids, found?: path (found away from its path: relative to the document, or by name in its folder), preview: true (showing the low-resolution preview, not the file), refused?: why the path is not followed (another computer, a device or a URL: it counts as missing)}], missing, modified}` |

| `links.updateChanged` | Update Changed Links | — | — | `{} read again the active document's linked files that changed on disk since they were last seen (size or modification time), whatever Preferences → File Handling → Update Links says; the desktop app looks every two seconds and follows that preference. | `links.info` | Link Info | — | — | `{id?} an image's or placed document's Link Info (default: the one selected) → image.info's fields (id, name, linked, link, colorMode, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, width, height) and status: ok\\|modified\\|missing\\|embedded, format, ppi: [x, y] (the file's), effectivePpi: [x, y] (at its placed size), scale: [x%, y%] (of its 100% size), rotation (degrees, counter-clockwise), placement: {preserve, align, clip}; linked images also fileName, location (its folder), page?, fileSize? (bytes), modified?, created? (ms since the Unix epoch), refused? (why the path is not followed); a placed document has document: true, pageWidth and pageHeight (pt) instead of pixels, ppi and colorMode, and its scale is of its artboard's or page's 100% size` |
| `links.placementOptions` | Placement Options | — | — | `{ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: the selected ones), preserve?: transforms\\|bounds (default)\\|fileDimensions\\|fit\\|fill, align?: topLeft\\|top\\|topRight\\|left\\|center (default)\\|right\\|bottomLeft\\|bottom\\|bottomRight (where the new art sits; not for bounds), clip?: false (clip it to the old bounds where it is larger)} how a file read again (links.relink, links.update) takes each image's place: transforms keeps its scale (relative to each file's 100% size), rotation and position; bounds stretches it into the old bounds; fileDimensions puts it at 100%, unrotated; fit and fill scale it proportionally to fit inside or cover the old bounds. | `links.findFiles` | Find Linked Files | — | — | `{folder?: an absolute path, ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: the active document's missing links), maxSeconds?: 60 (1 to 600), stop?: false (true: stop the last search)} with folder: look in it and its subfolders, on separate threads, for files with the names of the linked files (in any letter case), and answer at once with the search's state (searching while it runs); without folder: the last search's state, with the files found so far. Each linked file's files come best first: same (the size and hash saved with the link), size (the saved size, where there is no saved hash or the file is larger than 1 GiB), then name. Within each kind, a file whose name has the link's letter case comes first. Then each file's folder names are compared with the saved path's, from the innermost outward up to the first one that differs, and a file with more matching names comes first; files that still tie are listed by path. Before the comparison, the saved path's parent-folder steps (.., or the empty components of a classic Mac :: run) are resolved, and . components in a slash path are skipped. A search looks for at most 1000 linked files and keeps the first 10 files of each one's name, and up to 10 that are the same file; it ends once every linked file has its same file, and searches only the folders text.findFontFiles may search, with the same maxSeconds, depth and count limits; none on the web → {id (absent while idle), state: idle\\|searching\\|done\\|stopped\\|failed, folder?, links: [{name, path, ids, files: [{path, size, match: same\\|size\\|name, caseDiffers?: true}]}], searched?: {folders, files, read}, skipped?, unreadable?, stopped?: stop\\|time\\|limit, error?, seconds?}` |

Transparency is flattened with the preset (EPS has none); the native document rides along in comments, for reopening the file as it was. Same as document.export {format: eps}` |

| `object.slice.make` | Make | Object › Slice | — | `{ids?} make each selected object (or ids) an object slice: its slice follows the object's bounds → {ids: the new object slices}` |
| `object.slice.release` | Release | Object › Slice | — | `{} release the selected slices: an object slice leaves its object as it was, a user slice becomes an unpainted rectangle; the objects end up selected → {ids}` |
| `object.slice.fromGuides` | Create from Guides | Object › Slice | — | `{} replace the user slices with the grid the ruler guides cut the artboards into (two vertical and two horizontal guides give 9) → {ids}` |
| `object.slice.fromSelection` | Create from Selection | Object › Slice | — | `{ids?\\|id?} a user slice over the visual bounds of the selected objects (or ids), selected → {id}` |
| `object.slice.duplicate` | Duplicate Slice | Object › Slice | — | `{dx?: pt (default 10), dy?: pt (default 10)} copy the selected slices as user slices with their options, offset by dx, dy; the copies are selected → {ids}` |
| `object.slice.combine` | Combine Slices | Object › Slice | — | `{} replace the two or more selected slices with one user slice over their bounds (the first one's options; object slices are released) → {id}` |

| `print.setup` | Print Setup | — | — | `{preset?: name ([Default] or a saved print preset, any case: print.presets.list; its settings replace the document's, as choosing it in the Print dialog does), settings?: {copies: 1 (1–999), collate: true, reverse, artboards: all\\|range\\|ignore (all the art as one page), range: "1-3, 5" (1-based, with artboards: range), skipBlank (leave out artboards with no art that prints), media: letter\\|legal\\|tabloid\\|a3\\|a4\\|a5\\|a6\\|b4\\|b5\\|b4 (jis)\\|b5 (jis)\\|b6 (jis)\\|japanese postcard\\|japanese double postcard\\|japanese envelope #3\\|japanese envelope #4\\|kaku #2\\|kaku #3\\|yonroku-ban\\|custom (a paper is named by its id or its dialog label, any case and spacing, so `B5 (JIS)` works; empty: all), margin: 0 (pt the device can't print around the paper: the imageable area is inside it), marks: {trim, registration, colorBars, pageInfo, kind: roman\\|japanese, weight: 0.25, offset: 6} (as document.exportPdf, at the paper's scale; empty: as they are)}, advanced: {printAsBitmap (composite pages print as one image each, at the document's raster effects resolution), overprints: preserve\\|discard\\|simulate (composite output; preserve writes them to overprint (/OP), simulate prints them as Overprint Preview shows them; | `window.taskBar.reset` | Reset Bar Position | — | — | `{} unpin the Contextual Task Bar and put it back under the selection` |

| `window.panels` | Panels Except Tools and Control | — | `Shift+Tab` | `{} show/hide the dock and the floating panels (hiding them closes a panel popped out of the icon column), leaving the toolbar and the Control bar as they are; returns whether the panels show` |
| `window.panel` | Show Panel | — | — | `{panel: id, toggle?: bool} e.g. layers, swatches, stroke (case-insensitive; display labels like "Layers" work too); toggle (the Window menu) hides a panel that shows, and shows it again where it was` |
| `window.panel.layout` | Change Panel Layout | — | — | `{action} serialized docking action, including floating geometry, divider sizes and accordion state` |
| `window.panel.move` | Move Panel | — | — | `{panel, anchor, zone?: tab\\|center\\|left\\|right\\|top\\|bottom\\|above\\|below, before?: panel, group?: bool, placement?} move a panel (with `group`, its whole group) into the group holding `anchor`: as a tab (before the `before` panel; null appends), a split beside it, or (`above` / `below`) a group of its own above or below it in its dock column or floating window; `placement` (a serialized Placement) replaces zone and before` |
| `window.panel.activate` | Activate Panel | — | — | `{panel} show and select a panel in its current group` |
| `window.panel.close` | Close Panel | — | — | `{panel} hide a panel` |
| `window.panel.collapse` | Collapse Panel Group | — | — | `{panel, collapsed?: bool} minimize the group holding a panel to its tabs (in a floating window, the window to its title bar), or restore it, as a double-click on a tab or the drag bar does; the same as window.panel.minimize {panel, minimized}. Without `collapsed` it toggles. Returns {panel, collapsed, layout}` |
| `window.panel.float` | Float Panel | — | — | `{panel: id or "tools", x?, y?, width?, height?, group?: bool, column?: bool or n, onto?: id, above?: id, below?: id, collapsed?: bool} float a panel (with `group`, its whole group; with `column`, its whole dock column or floating window) as a floating window with its top-left corner at x, y in window points (default: inside the dock area, cascaded), as dragging its tab out does; a whole floating window keeps its rect unless given one. `onto` makes it a tab of the floating group holding that panel instead; `above` / `below` a group of its own above or below the group holding that panel, in its floating window or dock column. `collapsed` then minimizes (true) or restores (false) its window or group. A hidden panel shows first. "tools" floats the Tools panel at x, y. Returns {layout, closed, floating}` |
| `window.panel.dock` | Dock Panel | — | — | `{panel: id or "tools", anchor?: id, zone?: tab\\|center\\|left\\|right\\|top\\|bottom\\|above\\|below, before?: id, group?: bool, column?: bool or n, side?: Start\\|End, onto?: id, above?: id, below?: id, icon?: bool, collapsed?: bool} dock a panel (with `group`, its whole group): with no destination a floating panel goes back where it floated from (else joins the first dock group) and a hidden one shows where it was; with `anchor` (or `onto`) in the group holding that panel, `zone` as for window.panel.move; with `side`, as a new innermost column of that dock (`column: true` then moves its whole dock column or floating window); `column: n` with no other destination docks its group, or the whole floating window it floats in, as a new dock column at that place (1: next to the icon column, counting inwards; `true`: innermost); `icon: true` puts it in a row of its own at the end of the icon column; `above` / `below` as a group of its own above or below the group holding that panel. `collapsed` then minimizes or restores its group. "tools" docks the Tools panel at the left edge of the window. Returns {layout, closed, floating}` |
| `window.collapseDock` | Collapse Panels to Icons | — | — | `{collapsed?: bool} collapse every expanded dock column to icons (true), expand the outer dock column, Properties \\| Layers \\| Libraries (false), or toggle the outer column (omitted), as the double arrow at the top of the dock does; returns the new state` |
| `window.brightness` | UI Brightness | — | — | `{brightness: dark\\|mediumDark\\|mediumLight\\|light}` |
| `window.workspace` | Workspace | — | — | `{name} switch workspace (Essentials, Essentials Classic, Painting, …): the one left keeps its layout changes, and the one switched to comes back as it was left (as saved if never changed)` |
| `window.workspace.reset` | Reset Essentials | — | — | `{} reset the current workspace to the way it was saved, dropping the layout changes made in it` |
| `window.workspace.new` | New Workspace… | — | — | `{name?} save the current layout` |
| `window.workspace.manage` | Manage Workspaces… | — | — | — |
| `window.workspace.delete` | Delete Workspace | — | — | `{name}` |
| `window.workspace.rename` | Rename Workspace | — | — | `{name, to}` |
| `window.workspace.list` | List Workspaces | — | — | — |
| `window.newWindow` | New Window | — | — | `{} open another view of the current document, with its own zoom, center, rotation, artboard and Outline or Preview, as a tab of its own (titled with the view's number, "Name:2") or, when the current view floats, in a floating window; it becomes the current window; the Arrange commands treat each view as a window; file.close closes the current view and the last view closes the document; returns {index, view}` |
| `window.arrange.cascade` | Cascade | — | — | `{} put every open document in a floating window of its own and stack the windows from the upper left of the document area to its lower right, 30 pt apart, in tab order, each fitted to its window, the current document's in front; on the desktop each is an OS window, on the web and Wayland a window inside the app's window; returns {floating} (document indices)` |
| `window.arrange.tile` | Tile | — | — | `{} show every open document and each further view of one (window.newWindow) at once, edge to edge in the document area, one pane each in a grid (columns: the square root of the number of panes, rounded up), each fitted to its pane; the current window's pane takes the tools, a click in another pane makes its window the current one; the tabs stay; windows floating come back under the tabs first; with fewer than two windows open the view stays as it is; returns {tiled, panes}` |
| `window.arrange.floatInWindow` | Float in Window | — | — | `{index?, view?, at?: [x, y]} move the current window, or document `index`'s view `view` (its current view without one; it becomes the current window), out of the tab strip into a floating window of its own, fitted to it, with the window's top-left corner at `at` (main window points) or else at the next place of a cascade; dragging a document tab more than 24 pt above or below the tab strip does this at the pointer; the window holding the current document takes the tools, a click in another document's window makes its document the current one; a document already floating stays where it is; returns {floating} (document indices)` |
| `window.arrange.floatAllInWindows` | Float All in Windows | — | — | `{} move every document under the tab strip into a floating window of its own, at the next places of a cascade; returns {floating} (document indices)` |
| `window.arrange.consolidateAllWindows` | Consolidate All Windows | — | — | `{index?, view?} show one document at a time again, under its tab, after Tile, Float in Window, Float All in Windows or Cascade; returns {tiled: false, floating: []}; with `index`, only document `index` (its view `view`, else its current view) goes back under its tab and becomes the current one, the other windows and Tile staying as they are, as when a document window is dragged by its title bar (an OS window by the tab at its top) onto the tab strip; returns {tiled, floating} (document indices)` |
| `window.nextDocument` | Next Document | — | `Cmd+F6` | `{} make the open document after the current one in tab order the current one, as a click on its tab does (after the last document it goes to the first, and from the Home screen to the first); each view window.newWindow opened is a step of its own; returns {index}, with `view` for a document with more than one view` |
| `window.previousDocument` | Previous Document | — | `Cmd+Shift+F6` | `{} make the open document before the current one in tab order the current one, as a click on its tab does (before the first document it goes to the last, and from the Home screen to the last); each view window.newWindow opened is a step of its own; returns {index}, with `view` for a document with more than one view` |
| `tool.select` | Select Tool | — | — | `{tool: id} (see tools)` |

| `ui.cropImage` | Crop Image | — | — | `{} show a crop box on the selected image (tool `cropImage`): it starts on the part over the image's artboard; drag its handles or inside it, then Enter or the Control bar's Apply crops the image to it (object.cropImage {rect}), Escape or Cancel leaves it as it is, both back to the Selection tool. tool.setOption {key: "rect", value: [x, y, width, height]} sets the box` |
| `effect.applyLast` | Apply Last Effect | — | `Cmd+Shift+E` | — |

| `ui.newSwatch` | New Swatch… | — | — | `{spot?, global?, group?: colour group name} open New Swatch for the active fill or stroke (dialog `newSwatch`, engine: swatch.new); a color opens as a spot color with `spot`, and as a global process color with `global` alone` |

| `ui.colorPicker` | Color Picker… | — | — | `{stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), artboard?: index (the picker is for that artboard's background color instead), color?: "#rrggbb"\\|[r,g,b]\\|{c,m,y,k}\\|{gray} (default: the proxy's color, or the artboard's color, white when it has none)} open the Color Picker (fields: hex or color, channel, webOnly, swatches); RGB, HSB and hex values use the working RGB space; OK runs paint.setFill / paint.setStroke, or artboard.setProps {index, color} for an artboard` |
| `ui.sampleScreenColor` | Sample Color from Screen | — | — | `{} or {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), picker?: bool (the open Color Picker instead)} show the system's color sampler (macOS; browsers with an EyeDropper) and answer at once; the color the person picks anywhere on the screen then runs paint.setFill / paint.setStroke (one undo step) or becomes the Color Picker's color (field `color`), converted from display sRGB into the working RGB space; Escape cancels it and the colors stay as they were. ui.inspect reports `screenSampler: true` until it answers. An error without a sampler, while one is open, or with `picker` and no Color Picker open` |

| `tool.options` | Tool Options… | — | — | `{tool: id} what double-clicking a tool button opens: hand → fits the artboard in the window (view.fitArtboard), zoom → 100% (view.actualSize), rotate\\|scale\\|reflect\\|shear → that Object › Transform dialog (dialog `rotate`, `scale`, `reflect` or `shear`; error `nothing selected` without a selection), selection\\|directSelection\\|groupSelection → the Move dialog (dialog `move`; the same error), gradient\\|magicWand → the Gradient or Magic Wand panel (window.panel), artboard → Artboard Options of the active artboard (dialog `artboardOptions`, fields index, name, x, y, width, height, showCenterMark, showCrossHairs; OK runs artboard.setProps, and with other artboards selected with the Artboard tool a new width or height goes to each of them too, in its `artboards` list, each resized about the reference point the form used for that size, or about its top-left corner when the size was set in the fields directly), flare → Flare Tool Options (dialog `flareOptions`, fields diameter and pathLength (pt), opacity, brightness, growth, fuzziness, longest, rayFuzziness, largest (%), rays, rings, direction (°), raysOn, ringsOn; OK runs tool.setOption {tool: "flare", values}: the next flare dragged out uses them, and a Flare click's dialog, which also has x, y and preview (on initially), previews one there and accepts it as one Undo step; Cancel rolls back the preview), lineSegment\\|arc\\|rectangularGrid\\|polarGrid → that tool's Tool Options, its click dialog without x and y (dialog kind = the tool id, `__toolOptions: true`; lineSegment: length (pt), angle (°), fillLine; arc: lengthX, lengthY (pt), reference (0–8), arcType: open\\|closed, baseAlong: x\\|y, slope (−100…100), fillArc; rectangularGrid: width, height (pt, the Default Size), reference (0–8), rows, columns, rowSkew, columnSkew (%), frame, fill; polarGrid: the same with concentric, radial, concentricSkew, radialSkew and compound for rows, columns, the skews and frame; OK runs tool.setOption {tool, values} and draws nothing: the next drag uses them (Fill Line, the arc's type, base, slope and fill, the grids' dividers, skews and switches) and a click's dialog opens at them), columnGraph\\|stackedColumnGraph\\|barGraph\\|stackedBarGraph\\|lineGraph\\|areaGraph\\|scatterGraph\\|pieGraph\\|radarGraph → Graph Type for the selected graph (dialog `command` running graph.setType; an error without one), typeOnPath\\|verticalTypeOnPath → Type on a Path Options for the selected type on a path (dialog `command` running type.pathOptions; error `nothing selected` without a selection, and the command's error when no type on a path is selected),symbolSprayer\\|symbolShifter\\|symbolScruncher\\|symbolSizer\\|symbolSpinner\\|symbolStainer\\|symbolScreener\\|symbolStyler → Symbolism Tools Options (dialog `symbolismOptions`, fields tool, diameter (pt), intensity and density (1–10), shared by the eight tools; OK runs tool.setOption {tool, values}), blend → Blend Options, perspectiveGrid → Perspective Grid Options, eyedropper → Eyedropper Options (dialog `eyedropperOptions`, fields sampleSize, pickUp, apply; OK runs eyedropper.setOptions), printTiling → resets the print tiling (print.tiling.set {reset: true}), warp\\|twirl\\|pucker\\|bloat\\|scallop\\|crystallize\\|wrinkle → that tool's Tool Options (dialog `liquifyOptions`, fields tool, width, height, angle, intensity %, usePressure, detail, simplify, simplifyOn, rate, complexity, horizontal %, vertical %, affectAnchors, affectIn, affectOut, showBrush; OK runs tool.setOption {tool, values}), pencil\\|paintbrush\\|smooth\\|blobBrush\\|eraser → that tool's Tool Options (dialog `freehandOptions`, fields tool and the options the tool keeps: fidelity (px for pencil and paintbrush, the same at any zoom; pt for smooth and blobBrush), fill, keepSelected (on for pencil and paintbrush, off for blobBrush), mergeOnlySelection (off), closeWithin and editWithin (px, 0 is off), livePreview (pencil, on: off draws a thin line while the stroke is drawn, and the path's fill and stroke on release), size (pt), angle (°, −180–180; 0) and roundness (%, 1–100; 100) of the eraser's tip; OK runs tool.setOption {tool, values}), livePaintSelection → Live Paint Selection Tool Options (dialog `livePaintSelectionOptions`, fields selectFills and selectStrokes (both on), color (the highlight color, #rrggbb or a layer color's name; #ff2a2a), width (the highlight's width, 1–20 px; 4); OK runs tool.setOption {tool: "livePaintSelection", values}; a color with an alpha part (#rrggbbaa or #rgba) is an error and OK changes nothing), livePaintBucket → Live Paint Bucket Options (dialog `livePaintBucketOptions`, fields paintFills (on) and paintStrokes (off), highlight (on), color (the highlight color, #rrggbb or a layer color's name; #ff2a2a), width (the face highlight's width, 1–20 px; 4; an edge's highlight is half as wide); OK runs tool.setOption {tool: "livePaintBucket", values}; a color with an alpha part (#rrggbbaa or #rgba) is an error and OK changes nothing), shapeBuilder → Shape Builder Tool Options (dialog `shapeBuilderOptions`, fields gapDetection (off), gapLength (pt, 0–72; 3), openFilledAsClosed (on), clickStrokeSplitsPath (off), pickColorFrom: artwork\\|swatches (artwork), cursorSwatchPreview (off), selection: freeform\\|straightLine (freeform), highlightFill (on), highlightStroke (on), highlightColor (#rrggbb or a layer color's name; #ff4f4f); OK runs tool.setOption {tool: "shapeBuilder", values}; a highlightColor with an alpha part (#rrggbbaa or #rgba) is an error and OK changes nothing), objectsOnPath → Objects on Path Tool Options (dialog `objectsOnPathOptions`, fields pivot (0–8, row by row from the top left; 4, the center) and rotate (°, −360–360; 0); Reset puts 4 and 0 back; Save runs tool.setOption {tool: "objectsOnPath", values}: the objects attached next use them, groups attached before keep theirs)` |

Without id: the highlighted row when a Layers panel row was clicked last, else the one selected object or group, else the one highlighted row, else the current layer. Several rows or objects, or a row the panel's search, filter or Show Layers Only hides, is an error and nothing opens → {id, name}` |

An index past the last set or action, or an empty name, is an error and renames nothing → {name}` |
| `ui.action.stepsIncluded` | Include Action Steps | — | — | `{set: index, action?: index, step?: index, included: bool, others?: bool} include or exclude the playback of every step in a set, every step in one action, or one step. With a step and others: true, leave that step unchanged and apply included to every other step in its action (Alt/Option-click). Invalid indexes change nothing → {set, action?, step?, included}` |
| `ui.action.new` | New Action | — | — | `{set: index, name, key?: 0-15, cmd?, shift?, color?: red\\|yellow\\|green\\|blue\\|violet} add an action named name (spaces trimmed from both ends) after the last action of the Actions panel's set at set (0 is the top set) and start recording into it; Stop Playing/Recording (ui.action.stop) ends the recording. key 1 to 15 is the function key F1 to F15 that plays the action (0 or null: none), with cmd (Ctrl, Command on macOS) and shift; color is its Button Mode color (null or "": none), which the panel does not show. Action function keys take priority over command shortcuts and preserve the command's binding. On Windows F1, Ctrl+F4 and Ctrl+F6 cannot be used. The set becomes current and the new action is selected. The panel's Create New Action button and menu's New Action… (dialog `actionNew` with set, name, key, cmd, shift and color) run this on Record. While an action is recording, and for an index past the last set, an empty name, or a key or color that is not one of these, it is an error and nothing is added → {set, action}` |
| `ui.action.options` | Action Options | — | — | `{set: index, action: index, name?, key?: 0-15, cmd?, shift?, color?: red\\|yellow\\|green\\|blue\\|violet} change the Actions panel's action at action in set (0 is the top set); its steps stay. name renames it (spaces trimmed from both ends), key 1 to 15 with cmd (Ctrl, Command on macOS) and shift sets the function key F1 to F15 that plays it (0 or null: none), and color sets its Button Mode color (null or "": none); a param left out keeps what the action has, and cmd or shift alone changes that modifier of its key. Action function keys take priority over command shortcuts and preserve the command's binding. The panel menu's Action Options… (dialog `actionSetOptions` with set, action, name, key, cmd, shift and color) runs this for the selected action. An index past the last set or action, an empty name, or a key or color that is not one of these is an error and changes nothing → {name, key, color}` |
| `ui.action.play` | Play Action | — | — | `{action: name, set?: name} play the Actions panel's action named action at the speed ui.action.playbackOptions sets; set names the set to look in (default: every set). Accelerated plays it as one undoable batch → what command.batch returns. Step by Step and Pause For play its first step now and the others one at a time, each its own undo step, until the last, ui.action.stop, or a step that comes due while a different document is active than after the step before → {results: [the first step's result], pending: the steps left}. An action with a stop, at any speed, plays up to the stop and waits until ui.action.continue or ui.action.stop; at Accelerated the steps between stops are one undoable batch each → {results, pending, atStop?: true when it already waits}. A name no action has, or one that more than one action in the sets looked in has, or an action played while another is still playing step by step or with pauses, is an error and nothing plays` |
| `ui.action.playbackOptions` | Playback Options | — | — | `{speed?: accelerated\\|step\\|pause, seconds?: 1-60} set how the Actions panel plays actions: accelerated (the default) plays every step at once, step plays one step at a time and draws the window after each, and pause waits seconds (a whole number, 1 to 60, VectorCraft's own range) between steps. A param left out keeps its value; the setting is kept with the UI preferences. Any other speed or seconds is an error and changes nothing. The panel menu's Playback Options… (dialog `actionPlayback` with speed and seconds) runs this on OK → {speed, seconds}` |
| `ui.action.record` | Begin Recording | — | — | `{set?: index} begin recording an automatically named Action N in the Actions panel's set at set (0 is the top set), by default the current set or the first set; with no sets, make Set 1. The set becomes current, and ui.action.stop adds the recorded action after that set's existing actions. An explicit invalid set or an existing recording is an error and changes nothing → {set, name}` |
| `ui.action.stop` | Stop Playing/Recording | — | — | `{} end the Actions panel's recording and keep its steps, in the action ui.action.new made for it, else in a new action after the last action of its set, as the panel's Stop Playing/Recording button does. It also ends an action playing step by step or with pauses, or one waiting at a stop, whose message box closes: the steps played stay and the rest do not run. With nothing recording or playing it changes nothing → {stopped}` |
| `ui.action.insertStop` | Insert Stop | — | — | `{set?: index, action?: index, step?: index, message?, allowContinue?: bool} insert a stop, at which a playing action waits and shows message. With set and action (0 is the top set or action), the stop goes into that action, after step, else after its last step; without them it goes into the recording in progress, after the steps recorded so far. message defaults to none, and allowContinue, which offers Continue in the message box, defaults to false. A stop in an action becomes the panel's selected step, and its action and set become the selected ones. An index past the last set, action or step, a param of another type, params that are not an object, or no action and no recording is an error and changes nothing. The panel menu's Insert Stop… (dialog `actionStopRecord` with message, allowContinue, set, action and step) runs this on OK → {set, action, step}, or {recording: true}` |
| `ui.action.continue` | Continue Action | — | — | `{} play on from the stop the Actions panel's playing action waits at, on the document active now, and close the stop's message box (dialog `actionStopMessage`): the next step runs at once, or at Accelerated the steps up to the next stop as one undo step. The panel's Play Current Selection runs this while an action waits. With no action waiting at a stop it is an error → {results, pending, atStop?}` |
| `ui.action.deleteStep` | Delete Action Step | — | — | `{set: index, action: index, step: index} delete one step, a stop or a command, of the Actions panel's action at action in set (0 is the top set, action or step). The steps after it keep whether they are excluded, and no step of that action stays selected. A Record Stop dialog open on that step closes, and one open on a later step of the action follows it up. A missing or invalid index is an error and changes nothing. Undo does not bring the step back. The panel's Delete Selection runs this for the selected step → {set, action, step}` |
| `ui.batchDialog` | Batch… | — | — | `{set?: index, action?: index} open Batch (dialog `actionBatch`) for the action at set/action (default: the first action of the first set); OK runs action.batch with the dialog's source, destination and overrides` |
| `ui.actionSet.save` | Save Actions… | — | — | `{set?: index, id?, path?} write the Actions panel's set at set (0 is the top set; default: the current set) with its actions to an action set file (.vcactions) at path, else a picked file named after the set (the web downloads it). id holds the panel's own set id, which its menu passes: the set with this id is saved wherever it is now, and set is not read. A set over 8 MiB as a file, with more than 1,000 actions or with an action of more than 10,000 steps is not written; the panel menu's Save Actions… → {path}` |
| `ui.actionSet.load` | Load Actions… | — | — | `{path? \\| data?: the file's text} read an action set file (.vcactions) at path, else a picked one, and add its set after the Actions panel's sets; a set named like one in the panel gets the next free number (Print 2), and the other sets stay. Files of another version, over 8 MiB, with more than 1,000 actions or with an action of more than 10,000 steps are refused; the panel menu's Load Actions… (disabled where there is no open dialog, the web) → {set: index, name, actions: n}` |
| `ui.actionSet.delete` | Delete Action Sets | — | — | `{sets?: [index], ids?: [id]} delete the Actions panel's sets at these indexes (0 is the top set), with their actions (default: the current set). ids holds the panel's own set ids, which its question passes: the sets with these ids are deleted wherever they are now, sets is not read, and when one of them no longer exists nothing is deleted. The panel's Delete Selection on selected sets (Shift-click adds a range) asks first, and OK runs this. A recording into a deleted set stops and keeps nothing. An index past the last set is an error → {deleted: n}` |
| `ui.actionSet.duplicate` | Duplicate Action or Action Set | — | — | `{set?: index, action?: index} copy the Actions panel's action at action in set (0 is the top set) to right after it in the same set; without action, copy set with all its actions to right after it (default: the current set). The copy is named after the original with " copy" added, a copied set gets an id of its own, and the copy is selected. The panel menu's Duplicate runs this for the selected action, else the current set. An index past the last set or action is an error → {set, action?}` |
| `file.showPackage` | Show Package | — | — | `{folder} show a package folder (file.package's folder) in the file manager → {folder}` |
| `docInfo.save` | Save Document Info… | — | — | `{path?, selectionOnly?, category?} write Document Info's text report (document.info {format: "text"}) to path, else a picked file (the web downloads it); with category (a document.info category id) only that category, else every category. The panel menu's Save… passes the category the panel shows and its Selection Only → {path}` |
| `ui.epsOptionsDialog` | EPS Options Dialog | — | — | `{path?, useArtboards?, range?, …document.exportEps options} open EPS Options (dialog `epsOptions`: fields = these options over the ones used last); OK checks them, remembers them and writes path (else asks). Export As… → EPS opens it too` |
| `file.saveForWeb` | Save for Web (Legacy)… | — | `Cmd+Alt+Shift+S` | `{} open Save for Web (dialog `saveForWeb`: fields = the webExport.settings settings, `preset` loads a preset, __view: original\\|optimized\\|2up\\|4up, __zoom, __kbps; Save… remembers the settings and writes the files, Done only remembers them); with settings = document.exportForWeb, written to path, else a picked file (the web downloads the files) → {path, files, bytes}` |
| `file.saveForWeb.browser` | Preview in Browser | — | — | `{…document.exportForWeb settings} write the HTML page and its images to a temporary folder and open the page in the default browser (desktop) → {path}` |
| `file.exportSelection` | Export Selection… | — | — | `{multiple?: false} collect the selected objects as assets (assets.add: one of them all, as one image; true: one per object) and open Export for Screens on its Assets tab with them checked → {assets: [asset id…]}; document.exportSelection exports the selection in one go instead` |
| `css.copy` | Copy Selected Style | — | — | `{scope?: selection\\|all (default selection), …css.selection options} copy the CSS of the selection (css.selection; all: css.generate) to the clipboard (CSS Properties panel) → {css, rules: n}` |
| `css.exportFile` | Export CSS… | — | — | `{path?, scope?: selection\\|all (default selection), …css.selection options} css.export written to path, else a picked file (the web downloads it), with the pictures of rasterized art next to it (CSS Properties panel: Export Selected CSS…, Export All…) → {path, rules, images: [path…], warnings (css.export's; the status bar shows the first)}` |
| `file.print` | Print… | — | `Cmd+P` | `{} open the Print dialog (dialog `print`: the print.setup settings, preset (setting it loads that print preset; Save Preset… saves them as one), printer, toFile; Print keeps the settings with the document and prints, Done (discard: true) only keeps them); with params {preset? (a print preset's name: its settings instead of the document's), settings? (over the document's or the preset's), printer? (print.printers name; "" the default), toFile?, path?, format?: pdf\\|postscript, level?, flattenerPreset? (as engine file.print)} print without it: the print-ready PDF (engine file.print) goes to the printer → {pages, printer, printed: true, warnings}; with toFile, a path or no printing here (no print service) it is saved as a PDF at path (else a picked file, the web downloads it) → {path, pages, printed: false, warnings}; a PostScript file (format postscript, or a .ps path) is always saved that way` |
| `print.printers` | Printers | — | — | `{} → {printers: [{name, default}] (the system's printers), service (printing is available; else Print saves a PDF), setup (print.printerSetup can open the printer settings)}` |
| `print.printerSetup` | Printer Setup… | — | — | `{printer?} open the system's settings of the printer (the Print dialog's Setup…; desktop)` |
| `ui.printPresetsDialog` | Print Presets… | — | — | `{selected?: preset name} open Edit → Print Presets (dialog `printPresets`, field `selected`): [Default] (protected) and the saved presets, with how the selected one differs from [Default]. New… and Edit… open the preset editor (ui.printPresetDialog); Delete, Import… and Export… run print.presets.delete / import / export` |
| `ui.printPresetDialog` | Print Preset | — | — | `{name?: a saved preset to edit \\| preset?: the preset a new one starts from (default [Default])} open the preset editor (dialog `printPreset`: the Print dialog's settings fields plus `name`); OK runs print.presets.save and returns to Print Presets` |
| `plugin.dialog` | Plug-in… | — | — | `{id: an object filter plug-in (plugin.list), params?: {…}} Object › Plug-ins: run the filter at once when it takes no parameters or params are given (plugin.run), else open its dialog (dialog `plugin`: a field per parameter, `__plugin` the id, live preview; OK runs plugin.run as one undo step)` |
| `ui.installPlugin` | Install Plug-in… | — | — | `{path?: a .wasm file \\| dataBase64?: the module, name?: the file name shown as its source (with dataBase64), allowHeavy?: bool (the user agreed to its heavy budget), grant?: [permission] (the permissions the user granted it), replace?: bool, hash?: the module's SHA-256 (as plugin.install)} install a WebAssembly plug-in (plugin.install); without a path pick one (the web opens the browser's file picker; File › Open of a .wasm installs it too). A plug-in that lists permissions the user hasn't granted it asks the user first, showing its name, id, version, file SHA-256 and what each permission lets it do, and so does a filter that asks for a heavy budget: OK installs it if the file still has the SHA-256 shown, Cancel installs nothing → plugin.install's result \\| {pending: "confirm"} while it asks` |
| `plugin.cancelRuns` | Cancel Plug-in Run | — | — | `{} stop every heavy filter running in the background (its progress window's Cancel): it stops at the next slice of its budget and changes nothing → {cancelled: n}` |
| `plugin.hideRuns` | Continue in Background | — | — | `{} close the progress window of the heavy filters running in the background; they go on, shown in the status bar → {hidden: n}` |
| `imageTrace.cancelRuns` | Cancel Image Trace | — | — | `{} stop every Image Trace running in the background (its progress window's Cancel): it stops at its next colour and changes nothing → {cancelled: n}` |
| `imageTrace.hideRuns` | Continue in Background | — | — | `{} close the progress window of the Image Traces running in the background; they go on, shown in the status bar → {hidden: n}` |
| `ui.checkScript` | Check Script… | — | — | `{path? \\| data? \\| dataBase64?, name?, includes?: true with a path} check a script written for the reference app without running it (script.check; with a path, the files its #include lines name are checked too) and show the report (dialog `scriptCheck`: `report`, script.check's result; Copy Report copies it as JSON); without a file pick one (the web opens the browser's file picker; File › Open of a .jsx, .jsxinc or .jsxbin file shows the report too)` |
| `ui.perspectiveGridDialog` | Define Perspective Grid… | — | — | `{} open View › Perspective Grid › Define Grid (dialog `perspectiveGrid`, prefilled from the grid: the fields of perspective.grid.define); OK runs perspective.grid.define` |
| `ui.perspectivePresetsDialog` | Perspective Grid Presets… | — | — | `{selected?} open Edit › Perspective Grid Presets (dialog `perspectiveGridPresets`, field `selected`): New… and Edit… open the preset editor (dialog `perspectiveGrid` with `__mode` edit), whose OK runs perspective.presets.save and comes back; Delete, Import… and Export… run perspective.presets.*` |
| `ui.savePerspectivePreset` | Save Grid as Preset… | — | — | `{} open View › Perspective Grid › Save Grid as Preset (dialog `perspectiveGrid` with `__mode` save, `name` a new preset name): OK runs perspective.presets.save with the fields` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset1.1` | One Point Perspective Preset 1 | — | — | `{} apply the 1. saved 1-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset1.2` | One Point Perspective Preset 2 | — | — | `{} apply the 2. saved 1-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset1.3` | One Point Perspective Preset 3 | — | — | `{} apply the 3. saved 1-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset1.4` | One Point Perspective Preset 4 | — | — | `{} apply the 4. saved 1-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset1.5` | One Point Perspective Preset 5 | — | — | `{} apply the 5. saved 1-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset2.1` | Two Point Perspective Preset 1 | — | — | `{} apply the 1. saved 2-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset2.2` | Two Point Perspective Preset 2 | — | — | `{} apply the 2. saved 2-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset2.3` | Two Point Perspective Preset 3 | — | — | `{} apply the 3. saved 2-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset2.4` | Two Point Perspective Preset 4 | — | — | `{} apply the 4. saved 2-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset2.5` | Two Point Perspective Preset 5 | — | — | `{} apply the 5. saved 2-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset3.1` | Three Point Perspective Preset 1 | — | — | `{} apply the 1. saved 3-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |

| `ui.perspectiveUserPreset3.5` | Three Point Perspective Preset 5 | — | — | `{} apply the 5. saved 3-point perspective grid preset (perspective.grid.preset)` |
| `ui.blendOptions` | Blend Options… | — | — | `{} open Blend Options (Object › Blend › Blend Options…, the Blend tool's double-click, Alt-click and toolbar button; dialog `blendOptions`: spacing smooth\\|steps\\|distance, steps, distance (pt), orientation page\\|path, preview) on the selected blend's options, previewed live: OK runs object.blend.options as one undo step; with no blend selected it sets what new blends start with` |
